# Adding a new member (onboarding)

What happens when an exec **adds a new member** to SPAN — from an accepted application or from scratch. The result is a new row in `members`, a Supabase Auth account they can use to log in, and a welcome email with a temporary password. The next step in the flow is the new member’s first login and registration form (covered in the next doc).  
---

## 1\. Where and how members are added

**What happens:** Members with the **registration** permission see the **Member Management** section in the dashboard. There they can click **Add New Member** to open a modal with the member form: first name, optional middle name, last name, optional **preferred public name** (how they appear on the directory, team cards, and blog bylines when set), email (often a SPAN address like `firstname.lastname@spanationwide.org`), original/personal email, role, active flag, start date, DOB, school, city, state, phone, LinkedIn, Instagram, notes, bio. **SPAN org email** is generated from **first + last name only** (middle and preferred names do not change the suggested address). The four permission checkboxes are only visible to execs; if you only have registration permission you can add members but not set their permissions. See figure.  
![][image1]  
*Figure: exec’s add member modal (actually scrollable; I merged screenshots for this one).*

**Typical paths:**

- **New form:** fill the member fields from scratch, or  
- **Import from an accepted application:** When they **Accept** an application (in the Applications section), the application is marked `accepted` and the **Add Member** modal opens with the form pre-filled from that application (name parsed from `full_name`, school, state, phone, social links, notes from additional info). The email field is often auto-filled with a generated SPAN email ([firstname.lastname@spanationwide.org](mailto:firstname.lastname@spanationwide.org)); the exec can change it. They then click **Add Member** to create the member.

After a successful creation, the UI shows a success message (e.g. “They will receive an email invitation to set up their account”) and the modal closes. The new member does **not** get an account until the backend has run (see below).

**Where it lives:**

- All of this is in **`src/pages/DashboardPage.jsx`**: the Member Management section, the “Add New Member” button, the Add Member modal, the member form state, and the submit handler. Import-from-application is handled by **`handleImportFromApplication(application)`**, which maps application fields to the member form and can be triggered from the application modal (“Accept & Add Member”) or from the “Import” action next to a pending/accepted application in the quick-add table. The SPAN email is generated by a helper (e.g. `generateSpanEmail(firstName, lastName)`); the form also has an effect that updates the email field when first/last name changes, unless the user has manually edited the email.

**Data:**

- **Table:** `members`. The form fields map to columns including **first\_name**, optional **middle\_name**, **last\_name**, optional **preferred\_name**, **email**, **original\_email**, **role**, **active**, **start\_date**, **dob**, **school\_name**, **city**, **state**, **phone**, **linkedin**, **instagram**, **notes**, **bio**, and permission booleans (**volunteer**, **applications**, **bills**, **registration**, **blog** where applicable). New members are created with **`registration_complete = false`** so they are prompted to complete the registration form on first login.  
- **Who can do it:** The dashboard only shows Member Management (and thus Add Member) to members who have the **registration** permission. The actual create is done via an RPC that runs with elevated privileges (see below), so the database doesn’t rely on RLS for this insert.

**Implementation notes:** New or renamed member fields need matching updates in the form state and the **`create_member`** / **`update_member`** RPC parameters. “Accept & Add Member” opens a pre-filled Add Member modal; creation still goes through **Add Member** and the RPC (not a single-click create). Editing an existing member uses Update Member / `update_member`, not this add flow. Display helpers for **public vs legal** naming live in **`src/lib/memberDisplayName.js`** (`memberSiteDisplayName`, `memberLegalName`).

---

## 2\. Backend: create\_member RPC and members-provision

**What happens:** When the exec clicks **Add Member**, the frontend calls the **`create_member`** RPC with all the form values. The RPC inserts one row into **`members`** (no Auth user is created in the database at this step). That insert is enough to trigger the rest: a **database webhook** (configured in the Supabase Dashboard) fires on `INSERT` to `members` and calls the **members-provision** Edge Function. The function then creates (or finds) the Supabase Auth user, links them to the member, and sends the welcome email.

So the flow is: **form submit → create\_member RPC → insert into members → webhook → members-provision → Auth user \+ email**.

**create\_member (database):**

- Defined in **`supabase/migrations/`** (e.g. `add_role_based_permissions.sql`, `fix_registration_complete.sql`). It’s a **SECURITY DEFINER** function so it can insert into `members` even though RLS would normally restrict who can insert. It does **not** create the Auth user; it only inserts the member row and returns the new member. It always sets **`registration_complete = false`** for new members so they see the registration form after first login.

**members-provision (Edge Function):**

- **Location:** **`supabase/functions/members-provision/index.ts`**.  
- **Trigger:** A **Database Webhook** in Supabase (Database → Webhooks) is set to run on **INSERT** on the **`members`** table and POST to the function URL. The webhook sends the new row (and metadata) in the request body.  
- **What it does:**  
  - Reads the new member record from the webhook payload.  
  - If the member’s email already exists in Auth, it links that user to the member and can send a “recovery” style email.  
  - If not, it creates a new Auth user (Supabase `auth.admin.createUser`) with a generated temporary password and sets `email_confirm: true` so they can log in right away.  
  - It updates the **`members`** row to set **`user_id`** to the Auth user’s id.  
  - Optionally it sets up **Cloudflare Email Routing** so the member’s @spanationwide.org address can forward to their personal email (original\_email).  
  - It sends a **welcome email** via **Resend** to the member (to their personal email if available, otherwise the org email). The email includes the temporary password and a link to the login page so they can sign in and complete registration. **Login itself uses the SPAN org email** (`members.email` / `@spanationwide.org`), not the personal address.

**Consistency:** New members are created with `registration_complete = false` so the first-login registration gate always runs for this path.

---

## 3\. Summary flow

| Step | Who / system | What |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Exec | Opens Member Management → Add New Member (or Accept & Add Member from an application). Fills or edits the form. |
| 2 | Exec | Clicks Add Member. Frontend calls `supabase.rpc('create_member', { ... })`. |
| 3 | Database | `create_member` inserts one row into `members` with `registration_complete = false`. Returns the new member. |
| 4 | Supabase | Database webhook fires on `members` INSERT and POSTs to the members-provision Edge Function. |
| 5 | Edge Function | members-provision creates (or finds) Auth user, sets `members.user_id`, optionally sets up Cloudflare routing, sends welcome email with temp password and login link. |
| 6 | Newly added member | Receives email, later goes to login page and signs in with temp password → sees registration form (next section). |

Next in the flow: **First login & registration** — the new member signs in, completes the registration form (required profile fields and profile photo), and then gets full dashboard access.
